Gives the handle of the desktop, the group that top level windows live in. Pass it as the group of [CreateWindow](CreateWindow). Windows without a group are always on it. With [ClientWidth](ClientWidth) and [ClientHeight](ClientHeight) it tells the size of the primary display. [DesktopBuffer](DesktopBuffer) does nothing here.

```blitzbasic
Graphics 320, 240, 32, 2
win = CreateWindow("Centered", 0, 0, 180, 100, Desktop(), 15)
SetGadgetShape win, (ClientWidth(Desktop()) - 180) / 2, (ClientHeight(Desktop()) - 100) / 2, 180, 100
Repeat
Until WaitEvent() = $803
```
@returns A handle that stands for the desktop.
@gap The windows are drawn in the program's own window, which has the size you gave `Graphics`, even though [ClientWidth](ClientWidth) and [ClientHeight](ClientHeight) tell the size of the primary display, with the area under the task bar and start menu. Windows cannot be placed outside of the program's window. Nothing can be drawn on or read from the desktop of the computer, see [DesktopBuffer](DesktopBuffer).
